title: Maximal geometric branch locus and its one-step blowup
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], Noetherian meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover), let $B\subset X$ be a normal crossings divisor, and let $D\subset B$ be a nonempty reduced union of irreducible components. A normal crossings divisor means a reduced effective Cartier divisor (its ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor) [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] which, etale locally [def-weil-etale-morphism], has equation $t_1\cdots t_r=0$ for distinct members of a regular system of parameters; a regular system of parameters in a regular local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ is a set of $\dim R$ elements generating $\mathfrak m$. For a geometric point $\bar x$ let $b_D(\bar x)$ be the number of local branches of $D$ at $\bar x$, equivalently the number of coordinate factors defining $D$ in such an etale chart. These numbers have a finite maximum $m\geq1$. The locus where $b_D=m$, endowed with its reduced closed subscheme structure $M$, is a nonempty regular closed subscheme of $X$. Etale locally at each point of $M$ one can choose the above parameters so that $D=V(t_1\cdots t_m)$, $B=V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ with $m\leq r$, and $M=V(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$. Let $b:X^+=\operatorname{Bl}_M(X)\to X$ be the blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] and $D^+$ the strict transform of $D$ [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Then $D^+$ is empty or a normal crossings divisor and $b_{D^+}(\bar y)\leq m-1$ at every geometric point of $X^+$.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.6 and 4.1.8, printed p. 118; local computation in 4.2.8--4.2.9, printed pp. 120--121. Geometric branches are used to make the normalization-fibre count precise.
